question: Compare the disclosed financing profiles of AGEL and APSEZ on debt maturity structure, interest-rate exposure and reliance on related-party or promoter funding, and say which shows more refinancing risk on the disclosed evidence.
scope: Requested comparison of AGEL vs APSEZ financing profiles (debt maturity structure, interest-rate exposure, related-party/promoter funding reliance) and a judgement on relative refinancing risk. The evidence corpus contains only Adani Green Energy Limited (AGEL) FY25 annual report excerpts (standalone and consolidated); no APSEZ filings are present. The comparison and the relative refinancing-risk conclusion therefore cannot be made on the disclosed evidence. This note records the AGEL-only facts that the excerpts support.

key_findings.text: Both specialists independently concluded INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE for the comparison: every excerpt supplied is from AGEL's FY25 annual report, and no APSEZ filing appears in the corpus, so no determination of which entity carries more refinancing risk is supported.

AGEL standalone contractual maturity profile of borrowings (including trade credits from banks, current maturities and interest accrued) at March 31, 2025: less than 1 year ₹8,280 crore; 1-5 years ₹14,493 crore; more than 5 years ₹nil; total ₹22,773 crore — i.e. no standalone borrowings maturing beyond five years and roughly 36% of the standalone total falling due within one year.

AGEL consolidated (Group) borrowings maturity profile (including current maturities and interest accrued) at March 31, 2025: less than 1 year ₹16,991 crore; 1-5 years ₹53,684 crore; more than 5 years ₹60,037 crore; total ₹1,30,712 crore — the consolidated profile is materially longer-dated than the standalone profile, with ₹60,037 crore beyond five years.

On interest-rate exposure, AGEL states that for FY25 there is no interest rate risk because the Company's borrowings during the year were mostly at fixed rates, whereas in the prior year exposure related primarily to floating-rate term loans from financial institutions/banks.

AGEL's interest-rate sensitivity analysis is run only on floating-rate non-current borrowings outstanding at the reporting date, using an assumed 50 basis point change, and only for instruments not hedged against interest rate fluctuations.

On related-party funding, AGEL discloses unsecured inter-corporate deposits (ICDs) from related parties bearing interest at 10.60%-11.00% p.a.; during the year the tenure of an ICD balance of ₹751 crore (originally due January 2026 and March 2026) was extended for a further 3 years, with an option for an additional 2 years, effective March 1, 2025.

AGEL states it has support from related parties (subsidiaries) to extend repayment terms of inter-corporate borrowings due to them, described as part of its liquidity management alongside monitoring debt and capital market funding options.
AGEL reports unsecured perpetual debt outstanding of ₹749 crore at March 31, 2025, unchanged from the start of the year with no issuances or redemptions during the year.

On a consolidated (Group) basis, AGEL's borrowings maturity profile (including current maturities and interest accrued) as at March 31, 2025 was: less than 1 year ₹16,991 crore; 1-5 years ₹53,684 crore; more than 5 years ₹60,037 crore; total ₹1,30,712 crore.
